paragraphs: This paper revisits how 3D Gaussian Splatting places and updates the Gaussians used to represent a scene. Existing approaches rely on carefully designed cloning and splitting rules, which can make rendering quality depend heavily on a good starting arrangement. The authors instead treat the Gaussians as samples from an underlying probability distribution representing the scene.

This perspective connects scene optimization to Markov Chain Monte Carlo. Adding noise converts the Gaussian updates into Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics updates. The authors also reformulate densification and pruning as deterministic transitions of the samples. Their replacement for cloning relocates Gaussians while approximately preserving sample probability, and an L1 regularizer encourages economical use of the available Gaussians.

On standard evaluation scenes, the method improves rendering quality, makes the number of Gaussians easier to control, and shows greater robustness to initialization. The contribution is a sampling-based account of both parameter updates and Gaussian placement, with practical benefits demonstrated in the reported evaluations.
neurips-2024-3d-gaussian-splatting-as-ma.tldr: Recasting 3D Gaussians as probability samples yields a rendering method with improved quality, controllable size, and greater robustness to initialization.

paragraphs: CLIP can struggle when a task involves specialized imagery or fine distinctions that were poorly represented during pretraining. This paper improves prompt learning by using natural-language descriptions as additional knowledge about those concepts. The descriptions can come from people or a language model, making them a source of guidance when labeled task data are limited.

A learned aggregator first combines the available prompts into a summary matched to each input image. A prompt generator then learns to produce an embedding that remains close to this summary while also reducing the task's training loss. The resulting Aggregate-and-Adapted Prompt Embedding combines information from descriptive language with adaptation to the downstream task.

The authors report competitive results across few-shot classification, visual question answering, and image captioning, with particular benefits for unusual and out-of-distribution examples. The approach also removes the language-model inference cost required by the compared baselines. These findings support transferring prompt knowledge into a learned embedding that can be used across different tasks and data distributions.
neurips-2024-aggregate-and-adapt-natural.tldr: AAPE combines descriptive prompts into image-specific guidance and learns prompt embeddings that help CLIP adapt without language-model inference costs.

paragraphs: Federated learning becomes harder when clients have different data and also experience different changes over time. This paper studies real concept drift: changes in the relationship between an input and its label, expressed as P(Y|X). The authors find that local classifiers play a central role in adapting to these changes, making their treatment important for collaboration across clients.

The proposed FedCCFA framework clusters local classifiers separately at the class level. It then builds feature anchors from these clusters to guide the alignment of clients' feature representations. Alignment adapts according to the entropy of each client's label distribution. This design responds to the finding that useful alignment depends on both the input-label relationship and the degree of data heterogeneity.

The reported experiments show significant improvements over existing methods across various concept-drift settings. The approach matters because it connects collaboration to class-specific classifier groupings while adjusting feature alignment to client data. It addresses changing label relationships and inconsistent feature spaces within the same framework.
neurips-2024-classifier-clustering-and-f.tldr: FedCCFA combines class-level classifier clustering with adaptive feature alignment to improve federated learning when clients experience different concept drifts.

paragraphs: A vision transformer's final image representation combines contributions from many internal components. Understanding which components capture features such as shape, color, or texture is easier in CLIP because its image and text representations share a space. This paper develops a framework for extending that style of interpretation to other vision transformers.

The framework automatically decomposes the final representation into contributions from different model components. It then uses a linear mapping to place those contributions in CLIP's representation space, where text can help describe their roles. A new scoring function ranks components according to their importance for a particular image feature, giving a way to identify relevant parts of the model.

The authors apply the framework to several transformer variants, including DeiT, DINO, DINOv2, Swin, and MaxViT. The resulting insights support image retrieval from descriptions or reference images, token-importance heatmaps, and mitigation of spurious correlations. The contribution is a common interpretation procedure that connects component-level image representations to language across multiple architectures.
neurips-2024-decomposing-and-interpretin.tldr: The framework maps individual vision-transformer contributions into CLIP space so text can help explain and rank their roles.

paragraphs: Facial-part swapping aims to transfer selected regions from reference faces while preserving the rest of a target image. Methods built for whole-face replacement often offer limited control over individual parts. FuseAnyPart addresses this finer-grained task, allowing facial regions from multiple people to contribute to a customized character.

Its central challenge is combining several references efficiently and coherently. A Mask-based Fusion Module assembles the selected facial parts into a complete face representation in latent space, where the model works with encoded features. An Addition-based Injection Module then introduces this combined representation into the diffusion model's UNet, allowing the generation process to use the assembled facial information.

The authors report qualitative and quantitative experiments supporting the method's superiority and robustness. The design matters because it gives the model an explicit stage for assembling reference parts before injecting them into generation. This provides a mechanism for the selective, multi-reference customization that whole-face swapping approaches handle poorly.
neurips-2024-fuseanypart-diffusion-drive.tldr: FuseAnyPart assembles facial regions from multiple references in latent space and injects them into a diffusion model for selective customization.

paragraphs: This paper investigates what determines whether neural networks substantially learn task-relevant features during training or remain in a comparatively lazy learning regime. The authors derive exact solutions for a minimal model that moves between these regimes. Their analysis focuses on how initialization variances and learning rates differ across layers.

These choices jointly determine conserved quantities that constrain the geometry of learning trajectories in both parameter and function space. The analysis extends to more complex linear networks and shallow nonlinear networks with piecewise-linear activations. A crucial distinction emerges: rapid feature learning in the studied linear networks requires balanced initializations, whereas nonlinear networks can learn features faster when unbalanced initialization favors earlier layers.

Experiments provide evidence that this unbalanced regime also supports feature learning in deep networks of finite width. Reported benefits include more interpretable early CNN layers, lower sample complexity on hierarchical data, and less time to grokking in modular arithmetic. These results motivate further study of layer-specific initialization as a way to encourage efficient feature learning.
neurips-2024-get-rich-quick-exact-soluti.tldr: Exact analyses and experiments show how layer imbalances can accelerate nonlinear feature learning, while revealing a different requirement in linear networks.

paragraphs: Recommendation systems represent entities using embeddings that feed into later prediction and decision-making components. This paper asks how relationships between those entities can shape the way their embeddings change during training. Its proposed mechanism, Structure-aware Embedding Evolution, or SEvo, encourages related graph nodes to undergo similar updates at each step.

SEvo places graph information directly into the embedding update process. This makes the optimizer a route for incorporating structure, with minimal reported computational overhead during training. The authors analyze convergence properties for SEvo and possible variants to justify their designs. They also show how the mechanism can be integrated into existing optimizers.

A highlighted version augments AdamW and corrects its moment estimates. It produces consistent improvements across the evaluated models and datasets, with the paper reporting state-of-the-art performance. These findings suggest that graph relationships can be useful at the level of training dynamics, extending the ways recommendation models can use structure beyond an explicit graph-neural-network module.
neurips-2024-graph-enhanced-optimizers-f.tldr: SEvo incorporates graph relationships into embedding updates, improving recommendation models through structure-aware optimizers.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to train diffusion models to sample from a target distribution specified by an unnormalized density or an energy function. The target is therefore described through a function assigning relative weights to possible outcomes. The goal is to learn a sampler that produces useful draws from that distribution.

The authors benchmark several inference methods built around diffusion processes. These include simulation-based variational approaches and off-policy approaches based on continuous generative flow networks. The comparisons clarify relative strengths of existing algorithms and challenge some earlier claims, making the benchmark itself part of the contribution.

The paper also introduces an exploration strategy for off-policy training that combines local search in the target space with a replay buffer. This pairs searching for useful target-space samples with retaining experience for subsequent training. Across a variety of target distributions, the strategy improves sample quality. The released methods and benchmarks provide a basis for further work on learned diffusion samplers for amortized inference.
neurips-2024-improved-off-policy-trainin.tldr: A benchmark of diffusion samplers identifies algorithmic tradeoffs, while local search with replay improves off-policy sample quality.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to evaluate and improve contextual-bandit policies using interactions already collected by a different behavior policy. A single estimated performance value does not express how uncertain that judgment is. The authors therefore use pessimism: they construct upper bounds on risk to assess a policy conservatively before selecting or learning it.

Their main theoretical contribution is a set of fully empirical concentration bounds for a broad family of importance-weighted risk estimators. These estimators adjust for the difference between the data-collecting policy and the policy being evaluated. Searching for a tighter bound motivates LS, an estimator that uses logarithmic smoothing to reduce the influence of large importance weights.

The authors prove that LS has a tighter bound than its competitors in the comparison they develop. That bound also leads to improved policy-selection and learning strategies. Experiments spanning evaluation, selection, and learning report favorable performance, supporting the practical value of designing an estimator around a conservative performance guarantee.
neurips-2024-logarithmic-smoothing-for-p.tldr: Logarithmic smoothing of large importance weights produces tighter pessimistic risk bounds and improves offline policy evaluation, selection, and learning.

paragraphs: Assessing a long factual answer requires checking many individual claims while accounting for how much useful information it contains. This paper introduces LongFact, thousands of GPT-4-generated questions spanning 38 topics, and SAFE, an automated evaluator. SAFE breaks responses into individual facts, searches Google for evidence, and reasons about whether the search results support each fact.

The authors also adapt F1 scoring to balance factual precision with response coverage. Precision measures the proportion of supported facts. Recall uses a configurable target for the user's preferred response length, making the aggregate score sensitive to both factual support and the amount of information provided.

Across roughly 16,000 facts, SAFE agrees with crowdsourced annotators 72% of the time. In 100 randomly selected disagreements, it wins 76% of cases, while costing over 20 times less. These are empirical comparisons, not universal accuracy guarantees. Evaluation of thirteen models from four families further finds that larger models generally produce more factual long-form responses.
neurips-2024-long-form-factuality-in-lar.tldr: LongFact and SAFE benchmark long-answer factuality by checking individual claims against search evidence and balancing accuracy with response coverage.

paragraphs: Multimodal models often handle visual tasks by converting their outputs into a format suited to a language model. This simplifies development, but the paper argues that it overlooks differences between visual tasks and can hinder perception learning. Lumen addresses this problem by separating shared visual understanding from the decoding needed for each task.

The shared stage learns fine-grained alignment between visual and language concepts. Its output serves as a common representation for all tasks considered in the paper. A second stage routes this representation to lightweight task-specific decoders, allowing outputs to reflect each task's characteristics. The authors report that these decoders require negligible training effort.

Experiments cover vision-centric benchmarks and visual question answering. Lumen matches or exceeds existing multimodal approaches across a range of vision tasks while retaining general visual understanding and instruction-following capabilities. The findings support an architecture in which common concept alignment supplies reusable information and specialized decoders turn that information into appropriate task outputs.
neurips-2024-lumen-unleashing-versatile-.tldr: Lumen combines shared vision-language alignment with lightweight task-specific decoders to improve perception while retaining general multimodal capabilities.

paragraphs: Language models can lose effectiveness when inputs extend beyond the lengths encountered in training. This paper examines that extrapolation problem through positional information. It analyzes why models without position encoding fail outside their effective range and investigates how carefully arranged position encoding can extend useful operation beyond that range.

The theoretical results establish that weave position encoding can improve extrapolation without additional cost. Building on this analysis, the authors introduce Mesa-Extrapolation. The method uses a triangular attention matrix organized into chunks and applies Stair position encoding to handle the final chunk. These are the concrete mechanisms through which the proposed method organizes attention and positional information.

The reported experiments show competitive performance together with substantially reduced memory requirements and faster inference. They also support the method's effectiveness for extrapolation. The contribution connects a theoretical account of positional encoding with a practical attention design, suggesting a scalable way to expand the lengths at which language models can operate effectively.
neurips-2024-mesa-extrapolation-a-weave-.tldr: Mesa-Extrapolation combines weave positional encoding and chunked attention to improve length extrapolation while reducing memory use and speeding inference.

paragraphs: Reconstructing a clothed person in 3D becomes difficult when objects or other people hide much of the body. The paper identifies complementary weaknesses in existing approaches: implicit methods can capture clothing detail but struggle with hidden regions or require aligned shape priors, while parametric body models provide complete shapes that may not align with the image.

The proposed pipeline combines a probabilistic SMPL body model with point-cloud diffusion. The body model generates several plausible shape hypotheses, which become conditioning information through continuous 3D representations. Diffusion then refines the distribution of 3D points using both those hypotheses and image features aligned to pixels, bringing body-shape guidance together with visible image evidence.

This combination produces detailed clothed reconstructions and fills in occluded body regions. Evaluations on CAPE, MultiHuman, and Hi4D report improvements over methods using SMPL, implicit functions, point-cloud diffusion, and combinations of them under synthetic and real occlusion. The approach uses multiple candidate shapes to guide reconstruction where the image alone provides incomplete evidence.
neurips-2024-multi-hypotheses-conditione.tldr: Multiple probabilistic body-shape hypotheses guide point-cloud diffusion to reconstruct detailed clothed humans from heavily occluded images.

paragraphs: Preference feedback can help image generators follow text prompts, but human-labeled datasets can be expensive or narrow in what they assess. This paper introduces VisionPrefer, a dataset built using multimodal language models as annotators. It aggregates feedback about prompt following, aesthetics, fidelity, and harmlessness, giving training a broader set of preference dimensions.

The authors train a reward model called VP-Score on this dataset. Its preference-prediction accuracy is reported as comparable to that of human annotators. They then evaluate the dataset's usefulness by applying two reinforcement-learning methods to fine-tune text-to-image generators, using the learned preference signal to guide training.

Experiments show significant improvements in text-image alignment for compositional generation and benefits across dimensions including aesthetics. The work also reports better generalization across image distributions than previous human-preference metrics. Together, these findings support AI-generated preference data as a promising source of supervision for image generation, with the evidence grounded in the evaluated reward model and tuning experiments.
neurips-2024-multimodal-large-language-m.tldr: VisionPrefer uses multimodal AI feedback across four preference dimensions to train rewards that improve text-to-image alignment.

paragraphs: Language models can generate unsupported content and often do not identify where their wording comes from. Retrieval-based language models address these problems using text stored outside the model, but can be slow and produce less fluent output. NEST introduces a way to incorporate retrieved text spans into generation while providing attribution to their sources.

At every inference step, NEST performs token-level retrieval. It combines model and retrieval information into a mixture distribution and identifies promising continuations in a corpus. An approximate speculative-decoding procedure then accepts a prefix of a retrieved span or generates a new token. This lets generation incorporate source passages of arbitrary length through the decoding process.

Across knowledge-intensive tasks, NEST improves generation quality and attribution rate over the base model, outperforms conventional kNN-LM, and competes with in-context retrieval augmentation. Applied to Llama-2-Chat 70B, it achieves a reported 1.8-fold inference speedup. The results connect source-aware generation with faster decoding in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-nearest-neighbor-speculativ.tldr: NEST retrieves and speculatively accepts source-text spans to improve language-model output, attribution, and inference speed.

paragraphs: Detecting what changed between images is a different challenge from identifying objects within a single image. This paper introduces AnyChange, which adapts the Segment Anything Model to change detection without additional training. The goal is zero-shot prediction that can extend to unseen kinds of change and unfamiliar data distributions.

The adaptation method, bitemporal latent matching, uses semantic similarities within each image and between images in SAM's internal representation space. Those relationships give the model a basis for detecting changes across the two times. A point-query mechanism also allows object-centered change detection, making it possible to direct the comparison toward an object of interest.

Experiments support the approach's effectiveness for zero-shot change detection. On SECOND, the authors report a new unsupervised result exceeding the previous state of the art by up to 4.4% in F1 score. They also report accuracy comparable to supervised change detection with one annotated pixel per image, showing the usefulness of very limited user guidance in their evaluation.
neurips-2024-segment-any-change-ca808022.tldr: AnyChange adapts SAM without training to detect changes between images, with optional point queries for object-centered comparisons.

paragraphs: Training algorithms can favor particular solutions even when no explicit regularizer tells them to do so. This phenomenon, implicit bias, helps explain why equal training objectives do not imply equivalent outcomes. The paper studies gradient descent on separable multiclass data, extending a theoretical discussion that has been developed more extensively for binary classification.

Existing binary analyses often assume an exponential-tail property of the loss. Multiclass results have been more limited and largely restricted to cross-entropy. The authors use the framework of Permutation Equivariant and Relative Margin-based losses to formulate a multiclass version of that tail property. The resulting class includes cross-entropy and additional losses.

Within this framework, the paper extends an established binary implicit-bias result to multiclass classification. Its proof closely follows the binary argument, showing how the framework helps connect the two settings. The significance is a broader theoretical account of optimization's preferences, with separability and the specified loss properties defining the setting of the result.
neurips-2024-the-implicit-bias-of-gradie.tldr: A multiclass exponential-tail condition extends implicit-bias theory for gradient descent beyond cross-entropy on separable data.

paragraphs: Rare-event prediction creates two difficulties for policy evaluation: events may take a long time to occur, and very small values require accuracy relative to their size. This paper compares direct Monte Carlo estimation with least-squares temporal-difference learning, or LSTD, for finite-state Markov chains. It asks how efficiently each can achieve that relative accuracy.

The authors prove a central limit theorem for the LSTD estimator and bound its relative asymptotic variance. The bound uses quantities describing how states are connected in relation to their transition probabilities. This connects estimation efficiency to the chain's transition structure and provides a way to analyze difficult rare-event settings.

Using the bound, the authors show that LSTD can maintain a fixed level of relative accuracy with polynomially many observed transitions even in settings where rare-event timescales and the corresponding Monte Carlo difficulty grow exponentially with the number of states. The result establishes a substantial possible efficiency advantage within the analyzed setting, rather than a universal claim about all rare-event problems.
neurips-2024-the-surprising-efficiency-o.tldr: For analyzed finite-state chains, LSTD can estimate rare-event quantities with polynomial data requirements where Monte Carlo faces exponential difficulty.

paragraphs: Spatial representation learning turns geographic data into representations that neural networks can use. Although the broader field includes many spatial formats, TorchSpatial focuses on encoding point locations. The paper addresses the need for a common framework and benchmark that can support the development and comparison of these location representations.

TorchSpatial brings fifteen established location encoders into a unified implementation framework intended to support scalability and reproducibility. Its LocBench benchmark includes seven geographically informed image-classification datasets and ten geographically informed image-regression datasets. These tasks provide a shared setting for examining how location encodings contribute to predictive performance.

The evaluation suite considers both overall model performance and geographic bias, including a new Geo-Bias Score. The authors use it to analyze differences among location encoders along both dimensions. This matters because an aggregate performance measure alone does not describe geographic bias. The contribution supplies tools and comparative evidence for studying location representations and spatial fairness together.
neurips-2024-torchspatial-a-location-enc.tldr: TorchSpatial unifies location encoders and benchmarks their predictive performance and geographic bias across geographically informed image tasks.

paragraphs: Graph neural networks learn by passing information between nodes, but relying heavily on the input graph's connections can restrict that communication. This paper proposes a dynamic mechanism that learns flexible communication pathways while keeping complexity linear. It introduces learnable pseudo nodes that act as intermediaries between the original graph nodes.

Both kinds of node are projected into a shared space where their spatial relationships can be measured. As their positions change, those relationships define evolving message-passing pathways. The resulting model, N², uses one recurrent layer repeatedly to generate node displacements and construct the pathways. Reusing the layer also shares parameters across these repeated operations.

Evaluation on eighteen benchmarks reports stronger performance than popular graph neural networks. The model also scales to large benchmarks and uses significantly fewer parameters for graph classification because of its shared recurrent layer. The findings support learning communication routes through moving representations and pseudo-node intermediaries as a practical way to loosen dependence on fixed input topology.
neurips-2024-towards-dynamic-message-pas.tldr: N² learns changing graph communication routes through pseudo nodes, achieving linear-complexity message passing with a shared recurrent layer.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether a model can become fairer without losing utility when training data provide no prior demographic information. That requirement matters because methods described as demographic-free may still rely on demographic knowledge. The authors study this goal under the name harmless Rawlsian fairness, linking it to the distribution of losses across training examples.

Their analysis connects the requirement to losses concentrated at a single value, described mathematically as a Dirac delta distribution. VFair pursues this direction by minimizing training-loss variance within the set of empirically optimal solutions. A tailored dynamic update works with both losses and gradients to move toward relatively fairer solutions while preserving utility.

The experimental distinction between task types is central. Regression tasks show significant fairness improvements without demographic priors, whereas classification tasks usually do not. The authors attribute this contrast to classification's quantized utility measurements. The findings therefore support the approach particularly for regression while identifying a task-dependent obstacle to achieving the same goal in classification.
neurips-2024-towards-harmless-rawlsian-f.tldr: VFair reduces loss variation among empirically optimal solutions, improving demographic-free fairness mainly in the evaluated regression tasks.

paragraphs: Training one vision transformer for several tasks requires balancing shared learning with efficient execution. The paper argues that rigid combinations of mixture-of-experts structures and low-rank adaptation can impede optimization and slow inference. Its EMTAL method transforms a pretrained transformer during training, then integrates the learned structure for efficient use afterward.

The training architecture, MoEfied LoRA, decomposes the transformer into a low-rank mixture of experts and uses low-rank adaptation to fine-tune parameters. A Quality Retaining mechanism addresses the fact that tasks can learn at different rates. It uses historical high-quality class logits to help prevent an already well-trained task from deteriorating as training continues.

Finally, a router-fading strategy integrates learned parameters into the original transformer to support efficient inference. Experiments on public benchmarks report superiority over state-of-the-art multitask approaches. The contribution combines architectural adaptation, protection against task-specific degradation, and inference reparameterization, addressing several sources of inefficiency within a single multitask-learning method.
neurips-2024-transforming-vision-transfo.tldr: EMTAL combines low-rank experts, retention of strong task predictions, and router fading for effective multitask training and efficient inference.

paragraphs: A medical multimodal model must coordinate several tasks whose training objectives can interfere with one another. Uni-Med addresses this interference in the connector that transfers visual information to the language model. Its architecture combines a universal visual feature extractor, a connector mixture of experts, and a large language model.

The connector uses a router and multiple projection experts to manage the visual-to-language mapping. This gives the model a way to handle competing task demands at the point where modalities meet. The model supports medical question answering, visual question answering, report generation, referring-expression comprehension and generation, and image classification.

Ablation experiments support the connector's effectiveness across the tested configurations, with reported average performance gains reaching 8%. The authors also analyze task interference through gradients and parameter statistics. Comparisons show competitive or superior metrics against previous medical multimodal models across diverse tasks. These findings identify the connector as a useful place to address multitask interference within a unified medical model.
neurips-2024-uni-med-a-unified-medical-g.tldr: Uni-Med uses a mixture of experts in its visual-language connector to reduce interference across six medical tasks.

paragraphs: Lightweight transformer models for single-image super-resolution must learn useful image features and determine which features are similar. The paper argues that optimizing both separately at every layer creates a difficult interaction. Unified Projection Sharing, or UPS, separates these responsibilities by giving all self-attention layers a common space for similarity calculations.

A learnable projection matrix defines this shared space. Each layer still learns its own image features, but projects them into the common space when modeling similarity. This preserves layer-specific feature extraction while sharing the representation used for comparison. The design targets the coupled optimization problem that the authors identify in compact super-resolution models.

Across popular benchmarks, UPS achieves reported state-of-the-art results relative to leading lightweight super-resolution methods. The shared projection space also shows encouraging robustness on unseen degraded and depth images. Further experiments report promising performance in real-world and classic super-resolution, denoising, and deblocking, suggesting that the same separation can be useful across several image-restoration tasks.
neurips-2024-ups-unified-projection-shar.tldr: UPS shares a learned similarity-projection space across attention layers to improve lightweight super-resolution and other image-restoration tasks.

paragraphs: Point-cloud detectors can turn 3D voxels into one-dimensional sequences, but this rearrangement disrupts spatial proximity. Transformer-based methods often divide those sequences into groups, and their quadratic complexity makes enlarging groups costly. Voxel Mamba uses a state-space model with linear complexity to process the whole voxel space as one sequence.

The group-free design aims to alleviate the loss of neighborhood information. A Dual-scale State Space Model Block adds a hierarchy that expands the receptive field along the sequence while capturing more complete local regions in 3D. Positional encoding also introduces implicit window partitioning within the group-free framework, further incorporating voxel location information.

Experiments on the Waymo Open Dataset and nuScenes report higher detection accuracy than state-of-the-art methods along with substantial computational-efficiency advantages. The design matters because sequence efficiency and spatial structure are addressed together: whole-space processing removes grouping constraints, while the hierarchy and positional information help preserve relationships that serialization would otherwise weaken.
neurips-2024-voxel-mamba-group-free-stat.tldr: Voxel Mamba processes all voxels in one linear-complexity sequence and adds spatial structure to improve 3D detection accuracy and efficiency.
